57787.name: Veranderende Visies: Hollandse kunst uit de zeventiende eeuw
57787.entryRequirements: voor studenten Geesteswetenschappen: een positief bindend studieadvies (BSA). Voor studenten van buiten Geesteswetenschappen: een voltooide propedeuse
57787.recommendedPriorKnowledge: Hoe we naar de kunst in de Hollandse zeventiende eeuw kijken en deze benoemen is voortdurend onderwerp van discussie en verandert steeds. In deze module leer je de belangrijkste kunstenaars kennen, maar ook de oude en nieuwe vragen, benaderingen, resultaten en kanttekeningen daarbij. Dit vak sluit aan bij actuele discussies en behandelt zowel de gangbare opvattingen als nieuwe visies op het unieke van de beeldende kunst in deze periode. Je leert begrijpen hoe het komt dat de Hollandse kunst zo divers is in genres en stijlen en waarom zowel de kwantiteit als de kwaliteit van de kunstproductie uitzonderlijk is. Tevens maak je kennis met de schaduwkanten van het meest bezongen hoofdstuk in de Nederlandse geschiedenis en hoe dit zichtbaar is in de beeldende kunsten. Befaamde kunstenaars zoals Rembrandt, Vermeer, Frans Hals komen aan bod, maar ook onderbelichte en onbekend gebleven tijdgenoten. Zodoende brengt deze reeks hoorcolleges de huidige stand van wetenschap in kaart en toont het de kansen voor nieuw onderzoek.

sourceUse: The dated full-time Programma credit grid controls the public overview. Its 12 EC restricted-course parent comprises a 6 EC named specialisation list and a 6 EC Art History elective. The separate 12 EC excursion and 12 EC research seminar have named choice lists. Each is kept as a restricted choice with examples. The introduction describes a 30 EC mobility semester; the grid establishes the full 36 EC year-three allocation. The public page’s broader discussion of choice does not override 6+36 EC of genuine unrestricted space.
components: Inleiding in de Westerse kunstgeschiedenis I
The first year also includes a zero-credit language diagnostic and tutorial support. Tutorials continue in years two and three.
Inleiding in de Westerse kunstgeschiedenis II
Inleiding in de Westerse kunstgeschiedenis III
A compulsory first-year field course for Art History students. Study artworks and buildings on location in Paris.
Kunstwerelden: kunst en kunstgeschiedenis in mondiaal perspectief
Choose one 6 EC specialisation from the published list. Options include medieval art, seventeenth-century Dutch art, architecture and design, and art after 1900.
Choose a separate 6 EC Art History elective. The guide lists options such as Aesthetic Dissent.
Choose one 12 EC excursion from Berlin and Potsdam, Florence and Rome, London, or Flanders. Complete the Art History first year before the second semester begins.
Choose a 12 EC Art History research seminar. Options include socially engaged art, medieval outsiders, art and tourism, and women in the early modern art market.
The curriculum lists 36 EC of free electives in year three. Up to 30 EC can be planned together for a semester abroad.
Complete the first year and compulsory second-year courses. UvA strongly recommends completing a research seminar first. The thesis workshop and individual thesis take place in the same semester.

progression.firstYear: The required language diagnostic and yearly Art History tutoring carry zero EC. The Paris field course is exclusive to students of the degree.
progression.secondYear: The dated course entries require positive Art History BSA for Kunst in Nederland, Kunstwerelden, Toegepaste kunstgeschiedenis and Benaderingen. Philosophy likewise admits students with a positive BSA in Art History. A passed Art History first year satisfies those requirements and the excursion entry requirement by the start of semester two. The listed medieval specialisation and Aesthetic Dissent are eligible after positive Humanities BSA. The excursion to Berlin and Potsdam is an example with German reading or translation-tool skills as recommended preparation.
progression.thirdYear: The first listed Artivism seminar requires a Humanities propedeuse and recommends introductory art history and cultural studies. Other options accept a positive Humanities BSA or completed Humanities first year; some recommend Philosophy of Science. The thesis requires a completed first year and compulsory year-two courses. Seminar completion is strongly advised and can precede the regular second-semester thesis; the workshop and individual project run concurrently in that semester.
progression.openElectives: The 6 EC in year two and 36 EC in year three are genuinely open. External courses need Examination Board permission. Normally no more than 12 EC may be at introductory level, subject to the stated minor and language exceptions. A minor, mobility or internship is optional.
